items.title: Karnataka HC refuses to quash case against news channel's MD, CEO for making allegations about Dy. CM and  Collector
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Monday refused to quash criminal case against a Tumakuru-based news channel's executives in connection with a YouTube video which allegedly portrayed Deputy Chief Minister Dr G Parameshwar as being in a relationship with Tumakuru District Collector Shubha Kalyan IAS. Justice V Srishananda rejected the petitions filed by Prajashakti Channel Managing Director Shabbir Pasha and CEO V Kusuma, seeking quashing of the criminal case. During the hearing, the Court took strong exception to the language employed by the petitioners and the insinuations made by them in the video. “The background voice in the program is yours. You are the one who said that the Deputy Chief Minister is in love with the District Collector. Would it be okay if somebody speak like this to the daughters of your house? Do you alone have protection of Article 21 of the Constitution? Don't they?” the bench asked. items.title: ‘Why did I let him come to Delhi?’: Families mourn and question the capital after PG collapse
items.summary: “His birthday is in October, he would’ve turned 20,” said Pushpa, Arpit Jahaj’s mother, recalling his last birthday, when the family surprised him with a silver bracelet. “His bracelet and neck chain were gone. I was able to identify my son only with the birthmark near his shoulder,” she said. Arpit, a second-year student at Delhi University’s Atma Ram Sanatan Dharm College, had returned to Delhi from his home in Madhya Pradesh on Sunday morning after spending Rakshabandhan with his family. By Monday afternoon, after the debris was cleared at the Satya Niketan collapse site, he was among the seven confirmed dead. Five others who were injured are receiving treatment. He had last spoken to his mother around 12:30 pm on Sunday. The family rushed to Delhi from their home in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh, after being informed of the incident by Arpit’s uncle who lives in Ghaziabad. At the AIIMS Trauma Centre, the waiting room was a daunting place. “We had to wait for a long time to see our son. The police made us wait,” said Pushpa.
